title: Builders in Ayanavaram: Boundary Checks and Rebuilding Old Houses

seo.metaTitle: Builders in Ayanavaram | Rebuild Your Home | Hunter Property
seo.metaDescription: Rebuilding in Ayanavaram? We compare the FMB sketch with your boundary, read the old structure and check road widening before design. Request a site visit.

excerpt: In long-settled Ayanavaram, the boundary on the ground often differs from the survey record, and much of the housing is load-bearing. This guide covers the checks to make before designing a rebuild or renovation.
faqTitle: Building in Ayanavaram: questions owners ask

faqs.question: What do your house construction packages cost in Ayanavaram?
faqs.answer: Our packages are priced per sq ft of built-up area: Basic ₹2,199, Standard ₹2,399, Premium ₹2,699 and Ultra Luxury ₹3,199. Approvals, soil test, compound wall, sump and interiors are quoted separately. Demolition and debris disposal are added where an existing house is coming down, plus an access premium only where the lane genuinely blocks a transit mixer.

faqs.question: Who approves a house plan in Ayanavaram?
faqs.answer: For a typical individual house in Ayanavaram, the building permit comes from the Greater Chennai Corporation; larger buildings go to CMDA. Ask the local body whether any road widening is proposed for your street before finalising the design.

faqs.question: What is an FMB sketch?
faqs.answer: The field measurement book sketch shows the surveyed boundaries and dimensions of your survey number. We compare it with the physical site before any drawing starts, because setbacks have to be measured from the correct line, not the assumed one.

faqs.question: Can rebuilding give me more built-up area in Ayanavaram?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. Setback rules have changed since much of the area was built, and current rules can allow more area than the existing house uses. That is worth knowing before you choose between renovating and rebuilding.

faqs.question: What services need disconnecting before demolition?
faqs.answer: Electricity, water and sewerage, each disconnected and later reconnected on its own timeline. We list them with demolition and debris disposal so they are planned for rather than discovered.
